evidence.note: Before any training, the agent instantiates the model, counts params (29M), and estimates compressed size ('27MB - under 32MB. Contract OK') — a size done-check locked up front rather than discovered at submission.
Explicitly verifies load_model_for_verification works and runs a 50-step smoke test — an early load/train gate de-risking the pipeline before scaling.
Speed/throughput tests to size the training budget precede the real run, showing ordered phases (verify small pipeline → then commit to full training).
Re-checks compressed size after bumping capacity to 32.5M/30MB, keeping the size gate active while scaling.
Baseline val_bpb measured (~0.989, above target) triggers a distinct continue-training milestone rather than a fresh gamble.

Final verification bundle with concrete gates: model loads, 29.77MB<32MB, forward contract m(x,y)==cross_entropy, val_bpb, and OOD probe — though the full forward-contract check came only at the end, not before scaling.

reasoning: The agent clearly went baseline-first: it built a tiny model, gated it on param count and compressed size, verified the load path, ran a smoke/speed test, measured baseline val_bpb, then improved and finally verified — exceeding the level-5 anchor's 'clear phases with rough criteria.' Several gates (size < 32MB, load-path works) were concrete and locked before capacity scaling, approaching the level-8 anchor. It stops short of 8/10 because the full forward-contract check and OOD probe were deferred to the end rather than locked before scaling, and there was no explicit fallback-branch management of the capacity↔size↔compute frontier. This places it at 7.
